items.title: Chow: Penang must maximise existing land to drive state revenue
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang must maximise its limited land resources by focusing on development with the greatest economic impact, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. The solution is here," Chow said when asked how Penang could overcome its land constraints. Chow said the state was continuously acquiring land and opening up areas for industrial and other uses, while rezoning rural areas as urban areas was another way to optimise land use.

items.title: Myanmar confirms nearly 309,000 Rohingya in Bangladesh, security issues delaying repatriation
items.summary: YANGON: Myanmar's military-backed government has verified that nearly 309,000 displaced people in camps in Bangladesh are former residents of the troubled Rakhine State, but repatriation will proceed only after security in Rakhine improves, the foreign ministry said. Myanmar says repatriation will begin only when security conditions in Rakhine State become more stable. Myanmar says repatriation is strictly a bilateral matter with Bangladesh.

items.title: DAP delegates have spoken, respect their decision, Kon Yeow tells Rafizi over unity govt stance
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — DAP central executive committee member Chow Kon Yeow today told Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli to respect the party and its delegates’ decision to remain in the unity government. Chow said this was a basic principle following Rafizi’s comments on the resolution adopted at DAP’s congress yesterday. “We ask Rafizi to respect DAP and the decision of its delegates.

items.title: Chow: Penang Third Link remains in 2040 state structure plan
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang's proposed third link remains on the cards, with the project included indicatively in the Penang Structure Plan 2040. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the proposed third bridge or undersea tunnel remained in the plan as the agreement for the project was still valid. "Many development areas or development zones are placed indicatively.

items.title: Chow: Penang's draft 2040 plan not perfect, public views welcome
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang's draft 2040 state structure plan is not perfect, and public views will be taken seriously before it is finalised, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the draft Penang State Structure Plan 2040 (Review) is open to scrutiny, with constructive views and proposals from the public and stakeholders needed to improve the document. On mobility, Chow said public transport development must keep pace with the state's growth.

items.title: Safeguarding Malaysia's Blue Economy
items.summary: A TOTAL of RM823.88 million is the estimated value of Malaysia's fisheries resources lost to the intrusion of foreign fishing vessels between 2020 and 2023. Addressing illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is not just an enforcement matter but an essential step in protecting Malaysia's natural capital. This is where maritime intelligence can introduce a vital new dimension to Malaysia's security efforts.

items.title: Kenanga maintains ringgit forecast of RM3.95 to US dollar by year-end
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd (Kenanga IB) has retained its ringgit forecast of RM3.95 to the US dollar by year-end, underpinned by resilient growth, a sustained current account (CA) surplus and record foreign-currency deposits. Meanwhile, Kenanga IB said Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to hold the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent through 2026. "Our 2026 baseline GDP growth forecast of 5.0 per cent and inflation forecast of 2.0 per cent also remain within Bank Negara's current projections," it said.

items.title: Penang’s undersea tunnel still on the map, draft plan keeps idea alive for 2040
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — The proposed undersea tunnel or third bridge linking Penang island to the mainland was included as an indicative proposal in the Draft Penang State Structure Plan 2040 (RSN Penang 2040), Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. He said the project remain in the draft plan as the agreement with the appointed company is still valid, although its eventual implementation would depend on development schedules. He said the draft RSN Penang 2040 should serve as a “compass” for the state’s development.

items.title: Ranau court fines duo RM3,500 each after Sabah police link their wrist marks to illegal militant Philippine group
items.summary: RANAU, Aug 17 — Two men were each fined RM3,500 by the Ranau Magistrate’s Court for being members of a Philippine organisation deemed illegal under the Societies Act 1966 – the latest in such cases in the district. Roy Martin, 35, a farmer, and Mohd Sharin Ibrahim, 40, a tyre mechanic, were charged under Section 43 of the Societies Act 1966 for being members of Kappa Rho Kappa (KRK), also referred to in the investigation as the Knights of the Right Keppers, a Philippines-based militant organisation. According to the case documents, a team from the D7 Criminal Investigation Department (JSJ) of the Sabah Police Contingent Headquarters, led by Insp Jesmera bin Bandong, conducted checks on the two men at the premises.

items.title: Century‑old Penang Hill railway gets track and roof repairs in scheduled January 2027 break
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — Penang Hill’s iconic funicular will take a short break from January 4 to 10, 2027 for its scheduled bi annual maintenance, Penang Hill Corporation (PHC) announced today. Service is set to resume on January 11. During the closure, visitors can use the jeep service operated by the Penang Hill Jeep Service Association near the Penang Botanic Gardens Department Office, or take existing hiking routes to the summit.

items.title: RM900,000 Bentley payout legal battle was about integrity, says businessmam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A businessman whose RM900,000 insurance payout for his Bentley was upheld by the Court of Appeal says his legal battle with MSIG Insurance (M) Bhd was ultimately about clearing his name. Inderpal Singh said he was deeply insulted by the insurer's suggestion that he had deliberately staged the accident to make an insurance claim. "The logic behind that suggestion was, frankly, absurd," he said.

items.title: No water for nearly two months, then a RM120,000 bill — Putatan condo dwellers ask why pay for water Sabah water utility was already treating
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — Residents of Kingfisher Putatan Condominium (KFP) are refusing to pay the more than RM120,000 bill for water delivered by privately-operated tankers when they endured 55 days without supply between April and May. Some said they had no choice but to purchase bottled water for drinking, washing, cooking, cleaning and other daily needs. Despite being located just south of Kota Kinabalu, Putatan has faced repeated water shortages since 2018.

items.title: Maybank to support Haier in Asean's smart energy solutions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) is collaborating with China's Haier Group to support the expansion of the latter's new energy platform and ecosystem across Southeast Asia. In a statement today, Maybank said that it has entered into a Heads of Agreement (HoA) with Haier Energy Sdn Bhd, to form a strategic partnership aimed at accelerating the adoption of smart energy solutions across the region. Under the HoA, Maybank will leverage its regional business banking platform, Maybank2E and its comprehensive suite of products and services to support Haier Energy's expansion and facilitate supply chain agility.

items.title: Affin Bank misses estimates as provisions rise, says CIMB Securities
items.summary: Despite provisions rising 142.2 per cent YoY, Affin's operating income grew 12.2 per cent, supported by a 17.4 per cent increase in fund-based income and a 3.4 per cent rise in non-interest income. NIM also improved three basis points YoY to 1.52 per cent, while the cost-to-income ratio fell to 63 per cent from 68.9 per cent. However, second-quarter net profit fell 5.9 per cent quarter-on-quarter as non-interest income declined 12.5 per cent and provisions rose another 14.4 per cent.

items.title: HLIB maintains 'Buy' call on CIMB, RM8.70 target
items.summary: The research house said the recommendation followed steady second-quarter earnings from CIMB Group's Indonesian subsidiary, CIMB Niaga. In a note, HLIB Research said CIMB Niaga's operations remained resilient, supported by stronger loan growth and broad-based non-interest income growth. "Loan growth accelerated to 6.6 per cent YoY, while asset quality improved markedly with gross impaired loans falling to 1.55 per cent," it said.

items.title: Sarawak forest fire in Daro enters eighth day, 4ha still burning
items.summary: DARO, Aug 17 — Firefighters are on their eighth day of working to extinguish a forest fire in Kampung Kut here, which has affected about 29ha of land. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said in a statement that firefighters are working to completely extinguish the remaining hotspots of the forest fire. Firefighters from the Daro fire station were deployed to three sectors during the operation.

items.title: Six Johor students secure places at top global universities
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Six Johor students secured places at the world's leading universities after excelling in their A-Level examinations under the state's flagship Biasiswa Orang Muda Johor (BOMJ). Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the six scholars, from BOMJ's second cohort, would pursue studies in fields including robotics and artificial intelligence, biochemical engineering, chemical engineering and computer science. Four have secured places at University College London (UCL), while another will study at the University of Manchester and one at the University of Pennsylvania.

items.title: Foreign buyers' exit from Malaysian stocks continues for second consecutive week
items.summary: The transportation and logistics sector recorded the highest net foreign inflow at RM103.8 million, followed by telecommunication and media at RM34.9 million and energy at RM19.7 million. Meanwhile, financial services recorded the largest net foreign outflow at RM469.3 million, followed by industrial products and services at RM121.2 million and consumer products and services at RM89.6 million. Meanwhile, Malayan Banking Bhd had the biggest net foreign outflows during the week, at RM293.8 million, followed by AMMB Holdings Bhd at RM114.6 million and Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd at RM104.2 million.

items.title: Analysts raise Malaysia growth outlook after Q2 GDP surge
items.summary: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) revised its 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecast to 5.3 per cent from 4.7 per cent previously, while Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) raised its projection to 5.4 per cent from 4.6 per cent. PublicInvest said growth was "relatively broad-based", supported by household spending, investment and stronger external demand. Public consumption also accelerated to 7.6 per cent from 4.1 per cent, while public investment increased to 6.3 per cent from 5.3 per cent.

items.title: Starting them young on healthy gut habits
items.summary: TAIPING: Healthy gut habits should be nurtured from a young age as the digestive system plays a crucial role in supporting overall health, beyond simply aiding digestion. Yakult (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd's Public Relations and Science Division associate director Mazlyn Mena Mustapha said awareness of gut health among Malaysians remained relatively low, partly because the gut was an aspect of health that could not be physically seen. She said gut health is also closely linked to the body's immune system, with about 80 per cent of the immune system located in the gut.

items.title: Kuching man loses RM104,310 after falling for WhatsApp scam from friend’s hijacked account
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 17 — A 49-year-old man here lost RM104,310 to a phone scam last week. Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the victim was contacted via WhatsApp from a friend’s number, but it turned out the account had been hacked and hijacked. “Having trusted the message, the victim then made four transfers to three different accounts from Aug 13 to Aug 15, amounting to a total sum of RM104,310.

items.title: DAP sets Anwar year-end deadline for AG-PP separation, PM term limit bills
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has been given until year-end to ensure key institutional reforms, including separating the roles of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor and limiting the prime minister's tenure to two terms, are passed. DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo said the party's decision to remain in the Federal Government must now be followed by concrete action on its core reform agenda. "I urge Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to take immediate action to realise these reforms.

items.title: Father breaks down in court as four charged with son's murder
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: The father of murdered businessman Low Kai Xian broke down in tears in court today as four men were charged with killing his son. The family told us that they leave it entirely to the court to decide the fate of those accused of killing their son," he said when met outside the court. The proceedings drew Low's grieving family to court as early as 7.45am, with several relatives waiting outside in the hope of seeing the four accused face the court.

items.title: Johor businessman’s body bound in net, dumped in river; four accused face murder charge
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Aug 17 — Four men were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here with murdering a businessman, whose body was bound and covered in a net before being found in a river earlier this month. The accused — S. Yogesvaran, 40; Lim Yong Ming, 26; N. Achutan, 32; and How Han Wei, 33 — nodded to indicate they understood the charge after it was read before Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno in Bahasa Melayu. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim appeared for the prosecution, while Yogesvaran, Yong Ming and Han Wei were represented by counsel S.J.

items.title: CAP calls for prosecution of 'Malaysian Epstein Class' over Tabung Haji scandal
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) has called for sweeping prosecutions after the Tabung Haji (TH) Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) exposed serious governance and accounting failures. The characterisation was made by CAP in a statement following the declassification of the RCI report into TH, which examined the institution's management between 2014 and 2020. Also detained were a company director and a former company director, both holding Datuk and Datuk Seri titles respectively, as well as four former senior TH management officers.

items.title: 1,040 seized plant saplings found infested with pests, diseases
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: A total of 1,040 plant saplings seized by the General Operations Force (GOF) in two operations here were found to be infested with pests or diseases and will be destroyed. GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the affected saplings were among 5,770 seized from two lorries yesterday. He said the seizure comprised 60 kenanga plants, 80 batik kaffir lime saplings and 250 ixora saplings, among others.

items.title: Johor targets 200,000 jobs from quality investments by 2030
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor is prioritising investments that create high-paying jobs, develop local talent and strengthen local businesses, rather than simply pursuing headline investment figures. Onn Hafiz said investments entering Johor must generate wider economic spillovers, particularly by creating opportunities for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), developing local vendors and companies, and strengthening domestic supply chains. He said the state government, through Invest Johor and the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA), would work closely with the Federal Government to attract more quality investments and high-value projects.

items.title: Malaysia's current account surplus to remain firm at 2.1pct of GDP in 2026 – Kenanga IB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd (Kenanga IB) expects Malaysia's 2026 current account to remain firmly in surplus, maintaining a forecast at 2.1 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), compared with 1.6 per cent in 2025. In a note today, the investment bank said Malaysia's external position should remain resilient despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainties from the conflict in Middle East. On Friday, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) announced that Malaysia's current account balance recorded a surplus of RM10.8 billion in Q2 2026, supported by a substantial increase in the goods surplus to RM40.7 billion.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM AUGUST 17, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Monday as investors took profit following gains in recent sessions. The FBM KLCI is expected to retain a positive bias this week, but within a relatively narrow range, supported by resilient domestic fundamentals. The index is likely to move within the 1,725 to 1,735 range today.

items.title: Pantai firefighters extinguish blaze on Jalan Kerinchi, BMW destroyed, Axia 30 per cent damaged
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — A BMW was destroyed and a Perodua Axia partially damaged after a blaze broke out at KL Gateway Mall, Jalan Kerinchi, last night. The Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call via the NG999 line at 9.53pm before dispatching six firefighters from the Pantai station to the scene, New Straits Times reported. Operations commander Mokhtar Ramli said firefighters found two vehicles at the scene — the BMW was completely gutted, while the Perodua Axia sustained about 30 per cent damage.

items.title: Maxis shares up 2.16pct in early trade
items.summary: Revenue increased to RM2.66 billion from RM2.56 billion previously, supported by higher device and service revenue. In a note, MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB) said its revenue forecast remains unchanged but raised its profit margin assumptions to reflect Maxis' latest cost structure better, in view of its continued efforts to improve operational efficiency. Echoing MBSB IB, Kenanga Investment Bank raised its FY26 earnings by 5.3 per cent.

items.title: Search for Indonesia quake victims underway on Independence Day
items.summary: The agency reported a 5.6-magnitude quake in Nagekeo region, near the initial epicentre, on Monday morning. SEARCH TO CONTINUE The search will continue on Monday, authorities said. The quake damaged around 500 homes, he said.

items.title: Mara Corp ex-CEO fails to overturn RM3.4mil court order
items.summary: A three-member Court of Appeal panel, led by Datuk Wong Kian Kheong, upheld the High Court's decision against Badlisyah, finding no reason to interfere with the lower court's findings. On May 20, 2024, the High Court ordered Badlisyah to pay Mara Corp RM3,468,215.42 and indemnify the company against expenses arising from industrial relations claims involving former employees. Twelve of the employees were appointed to senior director positions, which the court found were beyond Badlisyah's authority.

items.title: Strengthen cycling regulations to protect all road users
items.summary: LETTER: The authorities must urgently introduce clearer guidelines, regulations and stronger enforcement on cycling activities on main roads and expressways to ensure the safety of cyclists and all other road users. Cycling on busy main roads can pose dangers not only to cyclists but also to motorists, especially due to the significant difference in speed. The lack of proper and connected cycling facilities has resulted in many cyclists turning to public roads, creating an increasing challenge that must be addressed.

items.title: Nanta: Four strategies identified to tackle contractor fraud
items.summary: Nanta said CIDB received 3,201 complaints between 2018 and 2025 involving contractors engaged in house construction and renovation, with most cases involving breaches of contractual agreements. "On average, CIDB receives about 600 complaints a year involving such issues. He said the breakdown of cases up to October 2025 included 130 involving breaches of contract, 86 related to construction quality and 50 involving unregistered contractors.

items.title: Air quality improves, Johan Setia still records unhealthy API
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality nationwide improved as at 10 am today compared with last night, with only Johan Setia, Selangor recording an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading. Meanwhile, 58 areas recorded moderate API readings of between 51 and 100, while another eight areas recorded good air quality with readings below 50. The API data are updated hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Four charged with murder of businessman found in river [WATCH]
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Four men were charged in the Magistrate's Court today with murdering a businessman whose body was found wrapped in a net and floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, on Aug 3. The four merely nodded after the charge was read before Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno. The four were jointly charged with murdering Low Kai Xian, 39, between an eatery in Jalan Emas Putih, Taman Sri Skudai, Johor Baru, and Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, between 2.35pm on July 29 and 12.30pm on Aug 3.

items.title: Jason Arday: UK academic who died amid plagiarism storm
items.summary: JASON Arday, the ex-Cambridge professor found dead amid a growing furore over claims of academic plagiarism and personal life embellishments, rose from humble roots in Britain to be hailed as an academic superstar. Boasting a backstory of remarkable achievement despite childhood autism and other developmental disorders, by the time of his death on Friday Arday was at the epicentre of intense controversy. Arday resigned from his Cambridge roles earlier this month after the university announced internal probes.

items.title: Asian shares mark time as Gulf war keeps oil prices up
items.summary: Brent crude was steady at US$88.50 a barrel after rising 6 per cent last week, while US crude slipped 0.3 per cent to US$82.12 a barrel, having gained 5.4 per cent last week. Australia's resources-heavy shares slipped 0.3 per cent. S&P 500 futures gained 0.1 per cent, having hit a record last week, while Nasdaq futures firmed 0.2 per cent.

items.title: Sarawak air quality improves as Serian and Samarahan drop from unhealthy to moderate
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 17 — Sarawak recorded moderate air quality at all monitoring stations except Bario, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading remained at good level as of 8am on Monday, according to the Natural Resources and Environment Board’s Daily Haze Watch. Air quality in Serian and Samarahan improved from unhealthy levels — with API readings of 157 and 151 respectively at 4pm on Sunday — to moderate levels of 98 and 92 by 8am. However, three areas recorded slight increases in API readings.

items.title: Man, 35, dies after motorcycle strikes lorry left without fuel on Tumpat flyover
items.summary: TUMPAT, Aug 17 — A 35-year-old motorcyclist was killed when his Yamaha 135LC struck the rear of a parked lorry on the Wakaf Bharu flyover here yesterday evening. The accident happened at about 5pm as the victim was riding from Kota Bharu towards Pengkalan Kubor, Berita Harian (BH) reported. Tumpat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Khairi Shafie said the lorry had been left on the left shoulder of the flyover after running out of fuel.

items.title: Religious leaders launch Tabung Haji RCI outreach, clarify misuse risks and safeguard 9.7 million depositors’ savings
items.summary: Former Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa said the initiative would see Islamic scholars and religious figures explaining the RCI TH findings through mosques, surau, schools, government departments, colleges, universities and community education platforms. He said the initiative followed a special conference, Hifz al-Mal, which brought together more than 100 scholars and religious leaders from across the country yesterday to discuss the findings and the responsibility of safeguarding the savings of 9.7 million depositors. “What makes the conference particularly significant is that it brought together religious figures alongside professionals and scholars from various fields, including chartered accountants, economic commentators, legal practitioners, religious educators and pondok scholars.

items.title: PM Anwar moves to amend Tabung Haji Act, vows stronger governance to safeguard Muslim trust
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — The government will amend the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) to ensure that the trust of Muslims continues to be safeguarded, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, also the Finance Minister, said the amendment was among the Madani Government’s measures to strengthen governance and ensure that every institutional weakness was addressed firmly. “Governance must continue to be strengthened, institutions cleaned up and every weakness firmly addressed.

items.title: Explained: Can a person be charged in a Malaysian hospital instead of a courtroom?
items.summary: Can an accused person be charged in a hospital ward? “Yes, the ward can be declared as open court and the proceedings can take place as if one was in the actual court concerned,” he said. Besides hospital wards, Sivananthan said a person could also be charged at other locations outside court.

items.title: Haze returns: What Malaysians need to know as air quality deteriorates
items.summary: Residents in several states, including Selangor, Negri Sembilan and Sarawak, are grappling with deteriorating air quality. As of Thursday (Aug 13) morning, air quality in 11 areas across the country was at unhealthy levels, with Sarawak the worst-affected state. Meteorologists have warned that without significant rainfall, the haze may persist, affecting air quality and public health across Malaysia.

items.title: Farmer’s coconut dehusking invention gets a shot at cracking the durian market
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 17 — An innovative coconut dehusking device developed by plantation entrepreneur Che Adnan Che Kadir, 56, which received a four-star rating, could now be adapted for durians and commercialised to meet the needs of the agricultural industry. Che Adnan said the judging panel at the Kelantan Department of Agriculture’s 2026 Agricultural Technology Innovation Competition proposed the idea after seeing the device’s potential for adaptation to other fruits. Che Adnan said he hoped that, once adapted for durians, the device could become a practical and safe home-grown innovation, while helping farmers and potentially reaching wider markets.

items.title: Mat Sabu launches book, warns Malaysians against propaganda, urges facts over allegations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Accepting allegations without proper scrutiny could fuel ‘asabiyyah’, a tendency to defend one’s own group even when it is at fault while viewing the good deeds of others negatively, said Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. He said the public should not accept information blindly, but instead verify the facts and gain a clearer understanding before taking a stand. Mohamad said facts and knowledge were often harder to accept and took longer to digest, unlike accusations and suspicions that could spread easily, especially through social media.

items.title: Malaysian pilot detained in Jakarta, accused of smuggling RM45m drugs abroad since 2024
items.summary: Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations found that the 39-year-old man is believed to have used his flight schedule to transport drugs to several destinations. “This was not the first time, because he had transported drugs to several countries on several occasions,” he said when contacted. Hussein said the interrogation also led to the discovery of the existence of several drug trafficking syndicate networks operating in Malaysia and abroad, including Indonesia.

items.title: Minister calls nine‑year abandoned Tambunan Hospital project ‘sick’, pledges RM988,000 for urgent upgrades
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 16 — The new Outpatient Department (OPD) building project at Tambunan Hospital, which has been abandoned for nine years, will be resumed to improve the comfort of patients and staff. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the situation at the hospital was among the most disheartening things he witnessed during his working visit there today, with patients and staff having to cope with limited space. Dzulkefly also announced an immediate allocation of RM988,000 to address urgent needs at the hospital, with a large portion channelled towards upgrading the Emergency Department.

items.title: USM climbs 149 places in Academic Ranking of World Universities, now Malaysia’s top university
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 16 — Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) has risen to become Malaysia’s top-ranked university in the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) 2026, climbing 149 places to rank 581st globally. USM said the achievement was significant as ARWU, also known as ShanghaiRanking, evaluates universities based on academic and research performance rather than reputation or perception alone. In ARWU 2026, USM recorded strong performance in the Publication (PUB) indicator, ranking 424th globally, while its HiCi indicator improved to 503rd worldwide.

items.title: Minister warns against immoral behaviour, stresses mosques and surau must remain sacred spaces
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Aug 16 — Muslims have been urged to observe proper conduct and good morals and refrain from immoral behaviour, especially in places of worship such as mosques and surau. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs), Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan, said mosques and surau are sacred places that must be respected and whose sanctity must be preserved. “I urge everyone to observe proper conduct, uphold good morals and comply with the law,” he told reporters after officiating at the closing ceremony of the Syariah Lawyers’ Sports Programme (SUKPES) at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) here today.

items.title: Kelantan Health Department to monitor baby girl’s growth after testing positive for drugs
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 16 — The Kelantan Health Department (JKNK) will continue to monitor the development of a baby girl who tested positive for drugs after birth to identify effects on her mental development, growth and physical development. JKNK deputy health director (Medical) Dr Rohana Daud said continuous monitoring is important to ensure any effects on the baby can be identified, and appropriate action can be taken at an early stage. “Based on the information obtained, the baby’s mother had taken tranquilisers, and its effects on the baby are unlikely to be prolonged.

items.title: Widow of corporal electrocuted in Sabah to receive Sarawak rental aid, housing support
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 16 — The widow of Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, who died in an electric shock incident in Sabah on August 6, will receive aid under the Sarawak Rental Assistance Scheme (SRAS), said Sarawak Deputy Minister for Public Health, Housing and Local Government Datuk Michael Tiang Ming Tee. The Pelawan assemblyman said he would assist Tang Wei Wei, 39, in securing an affordable home, in addition to providing rental assistance under the scheme. Meanwhile, he said the government would bear the pre-school education expenses, including textbooks, for Tang’s youngest child, who is four years old.

items.title: MACC arrests two policemen over RM14,000 traffic offence bribes on East Coast Expressway
items.summary: “Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect is believed to have conspired to commit the act with another patrol police officer between January and July 2026. Meanwhile, the male patrol police officer in his 30s who was previously arrested on August 11 has had his remand extended by four days until August 19. The remand extension order was issued by the same Magistrate today after the first remand application for the police officer expired today.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution warns poverty and drugs, not racial fears, are Malays’ real enemies
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — The position of Malays in the country is not threatened by the existence of other races, but by poverty and social problems such as drug addiction, said Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. The Home Minister said the real threat to the Malays is when they continue to be plagued by poverty and serious drug addiction. Malays are not under threat because there are Chinese in this country.

items.title: Three towns choke on unhealthy API, Serian tops list as haze blankets Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Three areas, including two in Sarawak, recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today. In Selangor, Johan Setia also recorded an unhealthy API reading of 124. Meanwhile, 65 other locations recorded moderate air quality levels.

items.title: Sarawak Education Department says Serian schools reopen tomorrow
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 16 — All primary and secondary schools under the Serian District Education Office (PPD) will operate as usual from tomorrow, the Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said in a statement today. “JPNS will continue to emphasise the welfare, health and safety of students, especially when facing hot weather or any unexpected weather conditions. 1 of 2019; Measures by the MOE to Ensure the Health and Safety of Students in Schools Located in Areas with Critical Haze Conditions dated Jan 15, 2019,” the statement said.

items.title: Saifuddin: End identity politics, focus on performance and economic recovery
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — PKR has called for an end to identity and racial politics, instead urging a greater focus on performance-based politics and economic recovery for the well-being of the people. “Malay identity, Islamic identity, Chinese identity, Indian identity, Sabah identity and Sarawak identity are all part of the reality of Malaysia. There is nothing wrong with identity.

items.title: Defend Malaysia’s ports, but identify firms abusing transshipment, says maritime expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Malaysia should firmly defend its reputation as a trusted trading and shipping hub while conducting thorough checks to identify companies that may be abusing its ports to circumvent United States tariffs, said maritime industry observer Datuk Seri Jeyenderan Ramasamy. He said Malaysia should neither dismiss the concerns raised by the US nor allow broad allegations to cast doubt on the country’s entire maritime and logistics sector, stressing that authorities should demand evidence and investigate specific companies and cargoes. Identify the companies and cargo involved.

items.title: Status quo for now, DAP delegates vote to stay in govt
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP delegates today overwhelmingly voted for the party to remain in the federal government until the end of the current parliamentary term. Congress speaker Cha Kee Chin announced that 1,857 delegates voted to stay, while 242 voted to leave the government. Loke said DAP would respect the 12 per cent of delegates who voted to leave the government, but the party must follow the decision of the 88 per cent majority.
